name: Notations Data Platform
description: The data platform beneath the estate (docs/PLATFORM.md): one canonical PostgreSQL layer — bitemporal, append-only, tenant-isolated by row security that is enabled and forced — an evidence index that describes objects and never holds their bytes, a transactional outbox, and rebuildable projections that hold no write grant on canonical truth. It is the fabric's anchor: a system binds to it under an authority its corpus role entitles it to, and the control plane refuses a projection that claims canonical state. It is real SQL in platform/sql and nine invariants checked against a running database, not a diagram; it is not yet deployed, and no tenant data lives in this repository. Model outputs and proofs land in object storage as evidence, which is where derived compute binds until a compute store is built.

capabilities.label: Append a canonical fact
capabilities.description: INSERT into canonical.entity, entity_alias, observation, assertion or relationship as the application role, under the caller's tenant. Every row is bitemporal and carries its admission or basis; an entity names the evidence object it was admitted from.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own admission, under forced row security; checked live by PLAT-005 and PLAT-006

capabilities.label: Close a fact's knowledge time
capabilities.description: UPDATE of superseded_at only: the one column the application may change on a canonical row. Nothing is deleted and nothing else is rewritten; a superseded fact stays readable as of the time it was believed.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own supersession; the trigger refuses any other column

capabilities.label: Index an evidence object
capabilities.description: INSERT into evidence.object: content hash, zone, rights, retention class, access scope, source system and retrieval time, all required. The bytes stay in object storage; the row describes them.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own capture, hashed before it is parsed; checked live by PLAT-007 and PLAT-009

capabilities.label: Quarantine an evidence object
capabilities.description: Place an object in the quarantined zone with a recorded reason; the consistency trigger refuses a quarantine without a reason and a reason without a quarantine.
capabilities.provenance: the caller's own decision, with its reason

capabilities.label: Claim outbox rows
capabilities.description: canonical.claim_outbox(batch_size): lease the next unpublished change rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so two relays never publish the same change and neither scans history to find the next batch.
capabilities.provenance: the outbox rows committed in the same transaction as the change they describe; checked live by PLAT-008

capabilities.label: Mark outbox rows published
capabilities.description: canonical.mark_published(ids): idempotent acknowledgement that a relay delivered the claimed rows. The publish boundary of controlled change; a broker is a second system and is not built.
capabilities.provenance: the relay's own acknowledgement of rows it claimed

capabilities.label: Record a projection build
capabilities.description: INSERT into projection.build: what was built, from which canonical revision, and the command that rebuilds it. A projection that cannot say this is not a projection.
capabilities.provenance: the builder's own record; the projection role holds no write grant on canonical or evidence (PLAT-004)

capabilities.label: Traverse relationships
capabilities.description: projection.reachable(from_entity, kinds, max_depth): the graph projection as a recursive CTE, depth-capped and cycle-guarded, returning each reachable entity once at its shortest depth. A graph database is admitted on a measured limit this cannot meet, never on its absence.
capabilities.provenance: canonical.relationship rows live at query time, under the caller's tenant

capabilities.label: Read current entities
capabilities.description: projection.entity_current: a materialized view of every live, unsuperseded entity, rebuilt from canonical state and rebuildable at any time.
capabilities.provenance: canonical.entity, folded at the last refresh; the view records nothing of its own

capabilities.label: Check the nine invariants live
capabilities.description: node platform/check.mjs: PLAT-001 through PLAT-009 against a running database — forced row security, no bypass role, a policy on every guarded table, no projection write grant, append-only canonical and evidence, bitemporal facts, complete evidence rows, the outbox and its backlog index, no bytes in evidence rows. Skips with a stated reason when no database is reachable; never passes by default.
capabilities.provenance: the live catalog of the connected PostgreSQL, not the migration files

capabilities.label: Apply the schema
capabilities.description: node platform/migrate.mjs [--reset]: apply platform/sql/*.sql in order to the configured database, then run the invariant checks. --reset drops the schemas first and is for development databases only.
capabilities.provenance: the SQL files in this repository, applied by the operator at the host

metadata.framework: PostgreSQL 16; PostGIS declared for the spatial projection
metadata.durability: managed PostgreSQL when deployed; a development cluster today

contracts.name: platform doctrine
contracts.summary: Six tiers in build order, the lean first footprint, what is deferred and the evidence that would admit it, and the nine invariants.

contracts.name: canonical schema
contracts.summary: entities, aliases, observations, assertions and relationships, bitemporal and append-only, with the notation:// URI as a domain.

contracts.name: evidence index
contracts.summary: Every object carries content hash, rights, retention, access scope and source; the bytes never enter the database.

contracts.name: row security
contracts.summary: Enabled and forced on every tenant table; application roles NOBYPASSRLS; the projection role holds no write grant on canonical or evidence.

resources.name: canonical database
resources.description: The canonical layer for every tenant when deployed. Losing it loses admissions and decisions that the evidence alone does not replay. Nothing of it is in this repository.

resources.name: evidence object store
resources.description: S3-compatible zones raw, quarantined, canonical_export and published_build. Indexed here, held there; the raw zone holds the class of capture that cannot be refetched.

resources.name: projection schema
resources.description: Rebuildable by definition (PLAT-004): if losing it would lose information, it is in the wrong schema.

environment.name: NOTATIONS_PLATFORM_DSN
environment.purpose: The PostgreSQL connection string the migration, the checker and the tests use. It may embed a password, so it is a standing grant to the canonical database and is treated as one.

reference.spatial: PostGIS is declared for the spatial projection; the development image carries no PostGIS extension and the checker reports the tier as declared, not installed.
reference.temporal: Every canonical fact is bitemporal: valid_from and valid_to are event time, recorded_at and superseded_at are knowledge time (PLAT-006).
open_questions: Where is the managed PostgreSQL deployed, and who holds NOTATIONS_PLATFORM_DSN? Nothing in this repository stands the platform up.

The audit log is append-only by trigger and grant but neither hash-linked nor signed (COR-008 fails): should the control plane's journal discipline move down into it, or should the plane's journal move onto it?
Temporal is declared for durable workflows and not yet run; the first workflow to need resume-after-failure is the one that admits it.
Derived compute binds to the evidence zones today because model outputs and proofs are objects; a compute store is admitted when a workload needs one.

corpus.holding: The canonical PostgreSQL schema for every tenant — entities, aliases, observations, assertions, relationships, permissions, audit log and outbox — and the evidence index beside it, with the nine invariants that hold them. Schema and checks only: no tenant data lives in this repository.

COR-001.note: The holding is the canonical schema and its extent is every table in canonical and evidence, named.

COR-002.note: structural: the platform holds canonical state on behalf of the systems that own it. Ownership is declared by the system that binds to it under canonical_state, and the control plane refuses a second owner; the store itself owns no domain.

COR-003.note: An observation carries its basis and value kind; an assertion its stance and what supports it; an entity the evidence object it was admitted from.

COR-004.note: valid_from/valid_to beside recorded_at/superseded_at on every fact, checked live by PLAT-006.

COR-005.note: structural: the platform answers no questions. It refuses writes by constraint with a named error; a typed refusal to an unanswerable question belongs to the system that answers from it.

COR-006.note: The quarantined zone with a required reason, and an entity's admitted_from, are the door; a serving projection has no write grant to walk around it.

COR-007.note: content_hash is required on every evidence object and checked to be a sha256; the row exists before anything parses the bytes.

COR-008.note: Append-only by grant and trigger, and audited, but the audit log is neither hash-linked nor signed: a consistent rewrite by a superuser would not be detectable.

COR-009.note: The projection role holds no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on canonical or evidence — the absence of a grant, checked live by PLAT-004.

COR-010.note: Evidence rows never hold bytes (PLAT-009), and no table carries a column for a person: the platform refuses to become the bucket or the profile.
